  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor (5 levels). Given the extreme right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81, sd=2.08), log-transform or use robust ANOVA (Welch's ANOVA) to handle heteroscedasticity. Alternative: Generalized Linear Model with Gamma distribution and log link.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean=0.73. Standard ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or binomial GLM. Report odds ratios relative to Sham reference.",
    "Path Efficiency: Bounded [0,1] with mean=0.47 but extreme outliers (max=29.8, 64× the theoretical upper bound of 1). Data quality issue suspected. Apply winsorization or filter implausible values (>1), then Beta regression or one-way ANOVA on logit-transformed values if bounded. If outliers are valid, use robust regression or quantile regression.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Check for right skew (max=75.35 vs mean=12.50). Consider log-transformation or Welch's ANOVA if variance heterogeneity across paradigms.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): Bounded [0,1] with mean=0.38, sd=0.24. Beta regression preferred due to bounded support. Alternative: one-way ANOVA with arcsine-square-root transformation, or linear model with logit link if zero-inflation minimal."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated by repeated measures—8 mice contribute multiple trials (n=76,655 total, 9,582 trials/mouse on average). Must account for non-independence via mixed-effects models or cluster-robust standard errors.",
    "Normality: QQ-plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals; severe non-normality expected for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency due to outliers.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test across 5 paradigm groups; likely violated given sd ranges and extreme maxima.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined n=48,846 vs Bright Visual Only n=3,323 (14.7× ratio). Welch's ANOVA or weighted regression recommended to handle unequal variances and sizes.",
    "For Success (binary): Check for complete or quasi-complete separation in any paradigm (e.g., Sham with n=3,505, success rate near 0 or 1).",
    "For Path Efficiency: Investigate data quality—values >1 indicate path length shorter than Euclidean distance (impossible without measurement error or definition clarification)."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus test significant (or GLM likelihood ratio test): pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for ANOVA models, or Tukey-adjusted estimated marginal means for mixed models.",
    "For unequal variances: Games-Howell post-hoc test.",
    "For logistic regression: pairwise odds ratios with Bonferroni or Holm correction for 10 comparisons.",
    "For mixed models: Kenward-Roger or Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, with Tukey adjustment on least-squares means.",
    "Focus contrasts: Combined vs each unimodal (ICMS Only, Dim Visual, Bright Visual) and vs Sham; ICMS Only vs Visual-only paradigms to test modality effects."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined paradigm (n=48,846, 63.7% of data) likely shows best performance: lowest Time-to-Target, highest Success, highest Path Efficiency, and lowest AD due to multimodal integration benefits.",
    "Sham (n=3,505, 4.6%) expected as poorest performer: highest Time-to-Target, lowest Success, highest AD indicating more erratic trajectories.",
    "ICMS Only vs Visual Only paradigms: unclear directional prediction without prior literature; may depend on whether intracortical microstimulation or visual cues provide more reliable spatial information.",
    "Dim vs Bright Visual: Bright Visual may show better performance if illumination improves cue visibility, or worse if overexposure causes distraction.",
    "Path Efficiency distribution uncertainty: if outliers >1 are erroneous, true efficiency likely higher than reported mean=0.47; if valid, indicates complex trajectory definitions."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe sample size imbalance: Combined dominates (63.7%), Bright Visual Only smallest (4.3%). Statistical power uneven; precision for rare paradigms substantially lower.",
    "Repeated measures structure ignored in standard ANOVA: 8 mice with ~7,000-11,000 trials each. Failure to model Mouse as random effect inflates Type I error.",
    "Path Efficiency data quality concern: maximum value 29.8 exceeds theoretical bound of 1, suggesting calculation error or unconventional metric definition. Cannot resolve without raw trajectory data.",
    "No covariates: Mouse identity, trial order, learning effects, and day/session effects unaccounted for.",
    "Temperature=0.25 and model=kimi are generation parameters, not experimental conditions—irrelevant to biological inference but noted for reproducibility.",
    "Summary-only data view: No access to trial-level distributions, precluding distributional diagnostics and outlier investigation."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for continuous outcomes and generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) for Success, with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect. Use Gamma LMM for Time-to-Target and Average Speed, Beta GLMM for AD, binomial GLMM for Success. For Path Efficiency, first clarify metric definition and validate/clean values >1, then apply appropriate bounded regression. Report marginal means with 95% CIs and paradigm-specific contrasts with multiplicity adjustment."
}
